ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a kind of delay switch. When S1 is opened, D will be released only after a delay of a period of time. This delayed release effect is produced due to the electromagnetic induction effect of which coil?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, a vertical iron core marked as F can be seen. Two coils are wound on the iron core: the middle-upper coil is marked as A, and its left side is connected to switch S1 and the power supply; the lower coil is marked as B, and its right side forms a circuit through switch S2. Above the iron core there is armature D, and its right end drives the contact to connect or disconnect circuit C. Reasoning: When S1 is closed, coil A is energized and makes iron core F become an electromagnet, attracting armature D downward. When S1 is opened, the current in coil A decreases rapidly, and the magnetic flux in iron core F also decreases accordingly. At this time, if the circuit where coil B is located is closed by S2, an induced current will be generated in coil B due to the change of magnetic flux; according to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by this induced current will hinder the decrease of the original magnetic flux, thereby maintaining the attraction of the iron core to armature D for a short time, causing D to be released with delay. Therefore the delayed release effect comes from the electromagnetic induction of coil B.
